title: Long-term SCN calcium signal recording in freely moving mice
protocol: Mix AAV-VGAT-Cre and AAV-FLEX-GCaMP7s at a ratio of 1:2 by pipetting.
Cut a small piece of parafilm and stick it on the adhesive slide.
Pipette 3 μL of virus mixture onto the parafilm.
Fix the AAV injection pump on the stereotaxic apparatus.
Pipette the AAV into the glass micropipette.
Mark the level of the virus suspension with an oil pen.
Anesthetize a 2-month-old C57 wild-type mouse with 2.5% isoflurane.
Maintain isoflurane concentration at 1.5% during surgery.
Fix the mouse's head on a stereotaxic apparatus.
Turn on the animal homeothermic system and adjust to 35°C.
Apply erythromycin ophthalmic ointment to the mouse’s eyes.
Cut hair from the mouse’s head with scissors.
Disinfect the scalp with 75% alcohol.
Make an incision to expose the skull.
Wash the surface of the skull with PBS.
Wipe the skull surface with 3% hydrogen peroxide.
Secure the skin of the head to the skull with 3M tissue adhesive.
Place a glass micropipette on the holder.
Dip the tip of the micropipette in oil pen ink.
Move the micropipette to the bregma point using the stereotaxic apparatus.
Lower the micropipette until it touches the skull surface.
Set coordinates (X, Y, Z) to (0, 0, 0) mm.
Move the micropipette up 1 mm to the left of the bregma point and lower it to read the Z-axis value.
Move the micropipette to the right of the bregma point by 1 mm and read the Z-axis value.
Continue adjusting the heights until the Z-axis difference is ±0.01 mm for both sides.
Return the micropipette to the bregma point and set coordinates to zero.
Move the micropipette upward and move it 4.2 mm to the lambda point.
Continue adjusting the heights until the Z-axis reading is ±0.03 mm.
Check if the left and right skull surfaces are still level after adjusting the anteroposterior axis.
Drill a hole with an 0.8 mm diameter drill at the bregma point of the mouse skull.
Carefully remove the dura with ophthalmic forceps to expose the central blood vessel.
Label the AAV injection site.
Move the glass micropipette to coordinates (AP -0.05, ML +0.15, DV 0) mm.
Lower the micropipette to the cortical surface and record the distance X between the skull surface and cortex.
Mark the recorded distance with ink.
Label the fiber implantation site by moving the glass micropette further right by 0.15 mm.
Lower the micropipette to the cortex surface and mark it with ink.
Add PBS dropwise to the puncture hole to keep it moist.
Mount the syringe pump containing AAV on the stereotaxic apparatus.
Move the syringe micropipette to the AAV injection site.
Zero the Z-axis coordinate and lower the micropipette to a depth of 5.85-X mm slowly.
Inject 150 nL of mixed virus at a rate of 50 nL per minute.
Leave the glass micropipette in place for 10 minutes after injection.
Slowly withdraw the glass micropipette.
Prepare an optical fiber tip with a diameter of 200 μm, length of 6 mm, and numerical aperture of 0.5.
Clean the exposed part of the optical fiber with 75% alcohol.
Remove residual alcohol from the optical fiber with sterile PBS.
Install the holder with the optical fiber tip on the stereotaxic instrument.
Rotate the holder to the left at an angle of 5 degrees.
Inhale PBS onto the cortical surface.
Move the optical fiber to the fiber implantation site and set the coordinates to zero.
Puncture the cortex of the fiber implantation site with a syringe needle.
Drop a small amount of PBS again.
Slowly lower the fiber tip to a depth of 5.65-X mm.
Aspirate the PBS on the surface of the skull and cortex.
Drop a small amount of 3 M tissue adhesive to fill the drilled hole.
Wait for the adhesive to completely turn into a solid.
Fix the fiber at the junction site of the fiber tip and the skull with dental cement (core fixation).
Fix the entire fiber tip to the skull surface with dental cement.
Minimize contact between the dental cement and the scalp.
Withdraw the optical fiber holder.
Put a dust cap on the fiber tip.
House mice in individual cages and wait 2–3 weeks for virus expression.
Wait 3 weeks for mice to recover after surgery.
Anesthetize the mouse with isoflurane.
Remove the dust cap on the mouse head.
Dock the fiber patch cord to the mouse head.
Place the mouse in the recording cage.
Add food and water to the recording cage.
Turn on the multi-channel fiber optic recording instrument and software.
Select the recording channel.
Set the sampling rate to 30 Hz.
Set the exposure time to 30 ms.
Adjust the gain to 10.
Set the 470 nm LED light power to 15%.
Set the 410 nm LED light power to 10%.
Select the interval recording mode with a recording time of 35 s and an interval time of 565 s.
Select the storage location for the record file.
Close the recording box.
Turn off the lights in the room.
Click record to start.
Minimize human activity around the instrument during recording.
Import raw data using Data Source in Inper Data Process software.
Remove invalid data with De-Inter.
Extract valid data using Extract Trend.
Display normalized calcium signal data by selecting deinter_MCorrected on the upper panel.
Display baseline reference signal of the 410 nm channel by selecting deinter_control_signals on the lower panel.
Screen mice for obvious rhythmic calcium signals within one day.
Record calcium signals for 9.5 days in screened mice.
Extract deinter_MCorrected data from normalized raw SCN calcium signals using SQLiteStudio software.
Store the extracted data in CSV format.
Visualize calcium signal data by PyCharm software and related codes (4-channels data, from c-1 to c-4).
Select the path of the CSV file in the 135 lines of code.
Change the storage path of the CSV file to be analyzed.
Change the format of the output image, including SVG and PNG formats based on True or False settings.
Adjust the frequency resolution for wavelet analysis of calcium signals.
Set the output file format and frequency resolution parameters in lines 157–167.
Run the code to output calcium signal visualization results and energy value files of calcium signals at different frequencies.
Adjust frequency parameters manually as needed.
Verify slice recording site under a dissecting microscope.
Anesthetize mice by intraperitoneal injection of sodium pentobarbital.
Lay the mouse on its back with limbs fixed on a foam board.
Open the mouse chest to expose the heart.
Insert perfusion needle into the left ventricle and fix it in place.
Cut the right atrium.
Perfuse the mouse with 10 mL of 1× PBS followed by 10 mL of 4% PFA solution.
Carefully remove the optical fiber and dental cement on the surface of the mouse skull.
Collect the mouse brain tissue and place it in 4% PFA for 48 hours at 4°C.
Cut 40–50 μm coronal sections with a Leica vibratome.
Place the sections in 24-well plates containing 1× PBS.
Observe under dissecting microscope to check for tissue defects at optical fiber implantation site.
Pick up brain slice where optical fiber was implanted.
Incubate brain slice in 1× PBS solution containing 10000× DAPI for 5 minutes.
Wash brain slice with 1× PBS for 5 minutes.
Add about 50 μL of 1× PBS dropwise to the adhesive slide.
Form droplets and spread the brain slices within them.
Remove excess droplets and air dry at room temperature.
Seal slides with 50% glycerol and nail polish.
Take pictures using a fluorescence microscope.
Obtain brain slices using a cryostat to check the optical fiber position.
Alternatively, process multiple brain samples using a vibratome.
